blocking.section: Decision drivers; Pros and cons of the options > OPA as an external decision service
blocking.issue: The ADR describes P3 as banning any network hop on the request path and says an OPA sidecar would violate it. P3 bans only dependencies on the control plane or on peers. It explicitly allows other remote calls before commit if they are declared on the Policy with a timeout and `failureMode` (pack section 8.7 rule 6). An OPA sidecar is neither Ruralz Control nor a peer Node, so the rejection rests on a misquoted principle.
blocking.evidence: ADR line 29: "- **No request-path network hop** (P3), and authorization always fails closed (P9)". Line 134: "- Bad, because every decision adds a remote call before commit, against P3, while embedding already gives prepared in-process queries". Vision P3: "No control-plane or peer dependency on the request path | ... Other remote calls, such as a Semantic Cache embedding call to an `AIProvider`, are declared on the Policy with a timeout and `failureMode` (P9)." Pack 8.7 rule 6: "Any other remote call before commit ... is declared on the Policy with a timeout and `failureMode`."
blocking.fix: Line 29: "- **No extra request-path hop**: P3 allows only declared, timed remote calls (pack section 8.7), and authorization always fails closed (P9)." Line 134: "- Bad, because every decision adds a declared, timed remote call before commit (pack section 8.7) that fails closed, while embedding already gives prepared in-process queries ([source](...v1/rego/rego.go))."
